successCriteria.description: All five model files exist at their exact declared paths (src/modules/employee/employee.model.ts, src/modules/leave-type/leave-type.model.ts, src/modules/policy/policy.model.ts, src/modules/balance/balance.model.ts, src/modules/audit/audit.model.ts), each exporting its entity type and the repository/service interfaces named in the phase scope.

Employee entity exposes exactly the fields id, employeeNumber, firstName, lastName, email, managerId (string|null), department (string|null), hireDate (Date), terminationDate (Date|null), and employmentStatus typed as the union 'ACTIVE'|'INACTIVE'|'TERMINATED'.
LeaveType.code reuses the shared LeaveTypeCode type imported from src/shared/types/ (not a duplicated inline literal), and LeaveType exposes name, isPaid, requiresManagerApproval, isActive.

balance.model.ts declares a local BalanceStatus type with exactly the members 'ACTIVE'|'EXHAUSTED'|'CLOSED' and the LeaveBalance entity carries totalEntitlement, usedDays, pendingDays, remainingDays, status, fiscalYear, createdAt, updatedAt.
AuditLog.action is the 7-value union 'CREATE'|'UPDATE'|'DELETE'|'APPROVE'|'REJECT'|'CANCEL'|'SUBMIT', and oldValues/newValues are typed Record<string, unknown> | null (never bare Record, never any).
Every shared type (LeaveTypeCode, DTOs, error classes) is imported from the src/shared/types/ barrel, and the phase compiles clean under strict TypeScript (tsc --noEmit) with no `any` usage.

constraints: This phase produces ONLY entity models + repository/service interfaces — no concrete repository/service implementations, no controllers/routes, no tests (those are parts 2 and 3).
Use `unknown` or typed unions for all dynamic values; never use `any` (HARNESS constraint no-any, severity high).
Import every shared type from the src/shared/types/ barrel (src/shared/types/ or src/shared/types/index), never from a generic or deep location.
Follow the task's single-file layout: each module's entity and its interfaces live together in the named *.model.ts file (no separate repository/service files, no barrels in this phase).
The five leaf modules depend only on shared-types in this phase; no cross-module imports (policy→leave-type is a later-phase concern).
outOfScope: Concrete repository implementations (PgEmployeeRepository, PgLeaveTypeRepository, PgLeavePolicyRepository, PgLeaveBalanceRepository, PgAuditLogRepository) — Phase 2 part 2.

Concrete service implementations (EmployeeService, PolicyService, BalanceService, AuditService) and the balance counter transition logic (reserve/approve/reject/cancel, negative guards) — Phase 2 part 2.
Jest unit tests for the five modules — Phase 2 part 3.
The leave module (LeaveRequest entity, countLeaveDays helper, orchestrator service, controller/routes) and the notification module — later phases.
Database migrations, SQL schemas, and any actual persistence wiring — this phase is type/interface-only.

entityInvariants.invariant: employmentStatus is restricted to the lifecycle 'ACTIVE' | 'INACTIVE' | 'TERMINATED'; managerId and department are nullable references, terminationDate is nullable and only meaningful when status is TERMINATED.

code is one of the six canonical LeaveTypeCode members (annual|sick|emergency|unpaid|maternity|paternity) and isActive gates whether the type may be used; isPaid and requiresManagerApproval are per-type semantics.

A policy references a leaveTypeId and defines entitlementDays; accrualRate, maxAccumulation, and minimumNoticeDays are optional (nullable) and isActive gates applicability; createdAt/updatedAt are tracked.

A balance is scoped to (employeeId, policyId, fiscalYear) and its status follows the lifecycle 'ACTIVE' | 'EXHAUSTED' | 'CLOSED'; totalEntitlement, usedDays, pendingDays are non-negative counters and remainingDays is derived (availableDays = entitlementDays - usedDays - pendingDays), never independently stored.

AuditLog is immutable (no lifecycle/mutation); every record captures entityType, entityId, one of the 7 actions, oldValues/newValues snapshots (Record<string, unknown> | null), performedBy (nullable), and performedAt.

interfaceConstraints.operation: IEmployeeRepository and IEmployeeService must be declared in employee.model.ts; the service exposes employee lifecycle operations (create/update/terminate/lookup) and the repository exposes persistence operations, both typed against the Employee entity.
ILeaveTypeRepository must be declared in leave-type.model.ts exposing typed persistence operations for LeaveType (create/update/find by code/find active).
ILeavePolicyRepository and IPolicyService must be declared in policy.model.ts; the service exposes policy lifecycle operations and the repository exposes typed persistence, both against LeavePolicy.

ILeaveBalanceRepository and IBalanceService must be declared in balance.model.ts; the service exposes balance operations (reserve/approve/reject/cancel/derive availability) and the repository exposes typed persistence, both against LeaveBalance.

IAuditLogRepository and IAuditService must be declared in audit.model.ts; the service exposes an append/record operation for state changes and the repository exposes typed persistence, both against AuditLog.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: LeaveType.code must reuse the shared LeaveTypeCode type (and its const object) rather than redeclaring the literal union.
Any DTO/error types referenced by the interfaces must match the shared shapes (LeaveBalanceDTO derived availability, AppError subclasses with code/statusCode) — do not redefine them locally.
Error semantics in service interfaces must align with the shared error contract (NotFoundError, ValidationError, InsufficientBalanceError, OverlapError) rather than inventing new error types.
Entity field names/types must match the reconciled architecture's domain_entities (Employee, LeaveType, LeavePolicy, LeaveBalance, AuditLog) exactly — no renamed or added fields.
Module directories and owned artifacts must match the reconciled module boundaries (employee, leave-type, policy, balance, audit under src/modules/).

integrationPoints.why: The sole dependency of all five leaf modules; LeaveTypeCode, DTOs, and error classes are imported from here.
Later phase consumes these entity/interface types to orchestrate submit/approve/reject/cancel across balance and audit.
Concrete repositories in part 2 will use the shared pool/optional client; interfaces must be shaped to accept an optional unit-of-work client as the last parameter.
